I can't determine B reliably from these three bands, so I'm not giving a full answer.

**What I can say:** For high-spin octahedral d⁷ (⁴T₁g ground state), the lowest band 9460 cm⁻¹ is ⁴T₁g → ⁴T₂g. The common weak-field relation ν₁ = 10Dq gives Dq ≈ 946 cm⁻¹. That relation is only approximate for d⁷ because the ground state mixes with ⁴T₁g(P), so the true ν₁ depends on B as well. The estimate is therefore a rough value, not a rigorous one.

**Why B isn't determined:** The other two bands (20 160 and 21 160 cm⁻¹) must be assigned to ⁴A₂g(F) and/or ⁴T₁g(P). I tried a 2×2 ⁴T₁g block model with a free assignment. It did not reproduce all three observed bands at a single (Dq, B) for either assignment, so I can't justify a B value from this data. A reliable answer needs a full Tanabe–Sugano / Racah energy-matrix fit with the band assignments stated explicitly. C does not enter the quartet-only levels, so it cannot be extracted from these bands either.
